summary: This section explains the powers and duties of a Company Liquidator when the Tribunal orders a company to wind up. The Liquidator can run the business, sell properties, handle legal cases, and settle claims, but must always follow the directions and control of the Tribunal. They can also take help from professionals and sign all necessary documents to complete the winding-up process.
points: The Company Liquidator can carry on the company business as needed for a beneficial winding up, subject to Tribunal directions.
The Liquidator has the power to sell movable and immovable property, actionable claims, or the whole undertaking.
The Liquidator can institute or defend legal proceedings and sign documents in the name of the company.
The Liquidator can invite and settle claims of creditors and employees and distribute sale proceeds according to law.
The Liquidator can borrow money using company assets as security and use negotiable instruments.
All powers of the Liquidator remain subject to the overall control of the Tribunal.
example: When Apex Trading Private Limited was ordered to wind up by the Tribunal, Mr. Roy was appointed as the Company Liquidator. To ensure a beneficial winding up, Mr. Roy decided to sell some movable property and actionable claims through a private contract. He signed documents in the name of Apex Trading Private Limited using the company seal. Later, he needed to settle claims of the company employees and distribute the sale proceeds. Since some funds were still required, Mr. Roy raised money on the security of the company assets. Throughout this entire process, he acted under the overall control of the Tribunal and sought its directions whenever necessary.

terms.meaning: A person appointed to wind up a company and manage its affairs during the winding-up process.
The judicial authority in charge of company law matters, such as the National Company Law Tribunal.
A claim to a debt or any beneficial interest that a person can recover through a civil court.
Documents like cheques, bills of exchange, or promissory notes that guarantee the payment of a specific amount of money.

watch: A Company Liquidator has wide powers to manage assets and settle claims, but every action remains subject to the control and directions of the Tribunal.
